## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit). 2026-11-24 (docs/DRIVE.md, drive-loader READMEs): drive-loader-ar2 0.12 and drive-loader-a4mk2 0.2 give mods a versioned +Drive payload API (drive_payload_abi, count, at, find, info with id, length and sha256, dl_payload_read; imported weakly by sidecar-core) and lock a loaded mod's file until the next boot: an upload over it is kept as <name>.new and swapped in at the next boot with the new CRC written first, so a power cut cannot leave the new file under the old CRC; the MODS page shows UPDATE or LOST and refuses DELETE (IN USE: RESTART FIRST). On the A4 reads that span a card sector go straight into the caller's buffer (a 4 KB read takes 7-10 card reads, not 64-80).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers. 2026-11-18 (changelog 2026-11-07..17, verification, machine guides): Octatrack base 0.7.7 skips stock's delay work for tracks whose delay is silent (CPU meter 41 to 34 % with DELAY on every track); a machine's CPU price is now its mean cost per playing track (FM Synth 0.1.4: 6 %, seven tracks a Part); DSP voices book only what the bank's Parts use (core 0 up to 3,120 cycles); a shared scale file for Octatrack modules. Rytm MKII: sets linked by Modwerk's own linker may use 704 KiB or 3.7 MiB of DDR above the 128 KiB mod area; the voices base drops the FX lock words (1,752 B more for modules). Rytm MKI SDK guide published (research). Digitakt II: the site builds Modwerk's base 8650bb8a on core-dt2 1.1 (elekloader#221 at 0df8409), downloads still off; new modules MIDI Engine (Rytm), Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (DT2), Vibrato (Octatrack, from octabam). Machine maintainers may now merge a machine's first module releases; pull requests that change a built package stay drafts until that build ran on a unit. The dialog saying the project's future is uncertain was removed. 2026-11-18, later (changelog, OCTATRACK_PACKAGE_DSP_HOOKS): Octatrack base 0.7.8 makes the per-track sound-source hook (DSP site 5) a chain (#1098): the base offers each track to every installed DSP track machine in turn and the first that owns it plays it, so a second DSP machine (BlackPyramids) can install over USB beside Analog BD; Analog BD's package and sound are unchanged. The key bus (option B) is merged (#737). 2026-11-19 (changelog 2026-11-14..19, DESKTOP_APP, MACHINE_RECIPE, HOOKS, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, arr-rows, butter- fingers, Digitone II verification): every contribution, core work included, now comes to Modwerk as a pull request, and every machine is to get a Modwerk base (Digitone II and Analog Four MKII included). Octatrack base 0.7.8 lets modules rest when unused; 0.7.9 adds a shared Part Edit menu and fixes an effect lost after a project load (I154). A desktop app (Electron, WebUSB and Web MIDI) is in development, Windows only so far, never run against a unit. Digitone II: core-dn2 0.3 builds booted on a second unit from Transfer, and stock 1.12 came back with a normal update; no Modwerk module can be built for it yet. Two stock Octatrack arrangement bugs found by Arr Rows (SB33, SB34). 2026-11-20 (changelog 2026-11-18/19, verification 2026-11-19 beta diagnostics, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machines guide, micro-timing README/TESTING, Digitone II GOAL): most of the day's changelog is web app, agent board and tooling. Octatrack: base 0.7.9 is the site's base since 2026-11-18 (about nine units by 2026-11-19); base 0.7.10 is to add a refusal code of its own when a module's DSP claims meet a delay buffer (code 12) and to log which check refused a module at start. The card holds two set slots (MODWERK0.SET, MODWERK1.SET); a set loaded from the card is made the one the next boot prefers while the other stays for recovery. A live CPU/DSP load card on the site (USB). The machine guide now explains the frame guard's budget and how to count skipped renders. New draft Micro Timing 0.1.1-experimental (own_mods); its remembered row moved out of battery RAM into the module's own memory. Zoom MS-70CDR: Sync repairs an effect missing from the pedal's list; the list is written back only while the pedal stays connected. Digitone II: Modwerk's own linker knows OS 1.12 and links core-dn2 0.3 and 0.4 byte for byte as elekloader does, but refuses mods with DSP code; the site builds no Digitone II firmware yet. Base changes now collect in one draft pull request per machine, shipped by the owner after long tests on a unit; device reviewers (assigned per machine) approve first module releases. 2026-11-21 (changelog 2026-11-17..21, verification 2026-11-19..21, OCTATRACK_USB_AUDIO_MODULE, TEST_PROCEDURE, DIGITONE_II_OS_RESEARCH): Octatrack base 0.7.10 gives a DSP claim that meets a delay buffer its own refusal (code 12, naming the FX2 slot to move), logs which check refused a module at start, brings Analog BD back after a rolled-back trial (I178), lets Undo finish once a module's page is closed, and cuts the UI-tick cost of large sets; 0.7.11 (served) waits for a project load to finish before it changes the DSP's effects (I180) and rests unused machine and effect modules; 0.7.12 (staged) installs USB Audio 0.3.0 as one module configured on the unit instead of seven base variants (reconnect failures fixed on the way, I176, I177). Installed but unused modules may cost at most 0.2 points of the frame interrupt from now on, or must rest. Every module or base change now goes through one test procedure that the submitter runs; reviewers only read its record. A fast MIDI soak and a queue for the shared unit are new tools. New modules: kitbank for the Digitone (OS 1.44) and Screen Off for the Octatrack; Improved SMPL 0.6.3 and Direct Jump Kyoti 0.2.0 (V7.3). Digitone II: the research page names the MCF5441x, the SHARC+ boot over DSPI2 and the ARM core; the site can read a development base and upload a module to its RAM, but no Digitone II module exists yet. Also 28 Zoom MS-70CDR effects (not an Elektron device). 2026-11-22 (changelog 2026-11-21, verification 2026-11-21, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_RESOURCE_GAUGES, TEST_PROCEDURE, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, effects guide, Grain, analog-bd and qperf docs, Rytm README): Octatrack base 0.7.13 judges a module machine pick on a busy unit by the CPU-meter points the machine adds (measured on a unit against Flex) instead of its frame price, which had refused Grain on a Part that played at 43.5 % on the owner's MKII. Module pages show measured CPU, DSP and memory figures where they exist and estimated tiers elsewhere. New track machine Grain (granular, up to six grains), measured at length on the owner's MKII; it still misses the frame deadline with 20-channel USB capture, and a panel freeze after one Grain trial is unexplained (I187). Under ot_emu the CPU meter reads 100 % from boot, so the emulator refuses every module pick. The effects guide explains the DSP56300 div half quotient. Rytm MKII: QPER Live Rec 0.3.0 follows pattern-length changes, BD ANALOG 0.2.2 drops the 808/909 badge, and Improved Performance (audio load 85.4 to 72.1 % on the author's unit) entered the library and was retired the same day, to be folded into the Rytm base. Every machine now runs one test procedure; Rytm unit steps run over its link with a RAM boot. Base work now goes to one cumulative draft per machine. 2026-11-23 (changelog 2026-11-22, verification 2026-11-22, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_AUTHOR_UPDATES, Grain README/TESTING, Rytm README, Pad Pressure Fix README): testers run released Octatrack base 0.7.13; one logged a UI stop during playback with six modules installed (I191), and a Windows tester saw failed USB staging and a USB Audio trial rolled back at the reconnect (I192); the installer now retries claiming the returning interface. Grain 0.1.2 treats the sample as a ring and plays each grain 3 dB lower. Rytm MKII: package builds refuse audio code that needs over 512 B of stack; Pad Pressure Fix moves into the base. An unpublished Elemod update can be rolled back. 2026-11-24 (changelog 2026-11-19..24, verification notes): base 0.8 admits modules by frame time instead of the mean meter (renders capped at 122 % of a frame) and holds late frame entries so the DSP skips a frame instead of stopping (I198, I199); a USB re-attach watchdog; LCD capture over USB at 5-30 fps; USB audio input; Part Edit rows can hide; sample-editor SNAP; restore outcomes named on the Status page; the site engine can upgrade a Digitone II's OS over USB MIDI (no UI yet). Base stock fixes: three are Zac-Kyoti's MIT code from octatrack-kyoti-fw, the USB input receiver is copied from octabam. Open: FM Synth 0.1.5 keeps costing about 11 frame points after its notes (#2030), RAM boots not seen by the host about 1 in 3 (#1985), a card-save failure after a Keep on 0.8, a 0.7.12 stall and UI freeze on a tester's MKI.

_Related: cites `elekloader` (README mentions elekloader (porting from it / hosted loader)); cites `octabam` (README: porting from octabam is part of the module guide); cites `octatrack-kyoti-fw` (sdk/machines/octatrack/elekloader/stock-fixes/README.md: three base stock fixes are MIT code from octatrack-kyoti-fw at 2cd3109); cites `octabam` (sdk/machines/octatrack/module-adapters/usb-audio-input-upstream/README.md: the USB input receiver is copied from octabam 382a478b) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### ems-octakit

Replaces four Parts per bank with 256 kits per project (OS 1.40C). Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### midisc-patcher

Browser patcher for the frozen 1.40MIDISC8.1 Octatrack OS (MIDI scene locks) from your OS 1.40C file. Licence: unspecified; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument.

_Related: builds on `midisc` (README: patcher for the 1.40MIDISC build) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### midisc

MIDI scene locks for Octatrack OS 1.40C. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument; README read 2026-11-11.

_Related: mod for `octabam` (README: built as octabam modules / with the octabam remixer) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### octa-panel

Real-time Octatrack emulator with sound and virtual panel in the browser, for testing OS 1.40C mods; built on octabam. Licence: MIT; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

_Related: copy of `octabam` (repo content is octabam (README, modules) as of 2026-10-13); uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: flash images are packed with elektron-firmware-tool); bundles `ems-octakit` (README: module table lists OCTAKIT from emuyia/ems-octakit); bundles `midisc` (README: module table lists MIDI SCENES from bkkbrls-del/midisc); bundles `octa-bt-pt` (README: module table lists LOFI AMF FIX from bryantysinger/octa-bt-pt); cites `octamax` (README: builds on or credits octamax's reverse engineering (passos: facts only, nothing copied)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01)_

### octabam

Modular Octatrack OS 1.40C "remixer": bus and track effects, FM synth machine, 255 kits, USB audio/MIDI, stock bug fixes. Base of Modwerk. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument; README, CHANGELOG and contributing docs read 2026-11-10. 2026-11-03: new midi-follow module (docs/site/usage/midi-follow.md, a test remix); not read further. 2026-11-10: WAVE (wavecf) is a 4-voice wavetable machine on the ColdFire, reduced from CHOMPI WAVE, heard on an MKII in builds W1-W6 (I58); XF CURVE offers 13 crossfader curves, run on a contributor's MKII on 2026-11-06; KEYBUS publishes each track's block peak for side-chain keys (make check only); a demand-loader soak with STEM REC froze an MKII (I57, open). 2026-11-12/13: new FRAME GUARD module holds a late frame interrupt out of a window in which the DSP's frame exchange stalls at START or a program change (I82); with it 32 first STARTs and 192 program changes ran clean on an MKII with a 20-channel USB capture. MIDI SCENES: CLEAR, COPY and PASTE SCENE act on the MIDI and audio locks together in either track mode, and a scene held across the MIDI key shows its locks as a fresh press does. 2026-11-15 (FAILURE_MODES, TRAPS, CHIP, MODULES): a program change to a demand effect that was not loaded stopped the audio in about two runs of three on an MKII while panel and USB still answered (I108); moving the loader's copy from the head to the end of DSP core B's frame cured it in 12 of 12 runs. A new gate lets a DSP instruction form ship only with a stock site, a register row or a module proven on a unit; a tool lists modules changed since their unit proof. 2026-11-16 (unreleased, 2026-11-14/16): REMOTE, an event ring a host reads over USB with PEEK and four commands; SCOPE and TUNER share the TEMPO key in the octabam remix; DRUMMER's KIT BALANCE takes step and scene locks; a LIM stereo peak limiter after MIX on RESONATOR and SHATTER; MIDI SCENES sends the Part's value when no scene locks a CC; SCALES keeps one audio scale per bank and Part; a ColdFire instruction-form check reports forms but refuses none yet. 2026-11-17 (CONTRIBUTING, remixes, TESTING): contributors' own remixes now live in remixes/community/<name>/ and may not use the octabam name; cxosc-core moved there. One module per pull request. CI runs one unit per gate job and skips units whose gates already passed for the same image. 2026-11-18 (CHANGELOG, TRAPS, firmware docs, module READMEs): PATTERN MUTE's per-pattern layer had been stored in byte 40 of each audio track record, which is the low byte of the one-shot trig mask; on an MKI a one-shot on step 1 or 2 read as a mute and an unmute deleted it (I146). The layer now lives in its own pmute.work side file and a 48-byte battery copy, and the double-FUNC switch ignores FUNC chords. DIRECT_JUMP_KYOTI V7.3 is pinned. New stock reading: SAVE PROJECT's job path, the PART window and its edit menu, the key-layer list per window, and the stock WAV header's RIFF size 8 bytes over the specification. 2026-11-19 (README, modules lazy-chop, src3-key, zoom-keep, CYCLE_SCAN, COSTS, CHIP, TRAPS): three audio-editor modules by a contributor, all on main and unreleased: LAZY CHOP slices a playing sample by tapping TRIG 1-16 (four pages, up to 64 slices, STUDIO and LIVE CHOP, ZERO SNAP, undo), SRC3 KEY starts and stops an SRC3-only recording with [MIDI] in the audio editor (MKI only), ZOOM KEEP keeps the editor's zoom per page; all three ran on the contributor's MKI (2026-11-10..14) with no issues found, ZOOM KEEP's across-tracks part in the emulator only. A new tool prices every module and stock effect from the DSP56300 manual's cycle table; against the unit's LOAD METER it reads about 3 % high on average (38 settings, 22 effects). 2026-11-20 (README, five new module READMEs and usage pages, FAILURE_MODES, HARDWARE_TESTING, TRAPS, DSP module READMEs): five new contributed modules, unreleased. From Hteah's ot-mods (entry ot-mods-hteah), ported by a contributor: PAGE LOOP (GRID REC: PAGE + trig 1-4 loops that page of the current track, in time), TRIG MUTE (hold a step + FUNC; the mute is kept as the trig's condition + 65, so stock plays such a trig and shows ERR) and TRACK TRIG MODE (CHROMATIC / SLOTS / SLICES per audio track, saved as a comment line stock skips); the readmes report each on an MKI in the author's ACCLOOP images since 2026-10-25/28, the octabam table grades them emulator only. By the LAZY CHOP contributor: LOCK EDIT ([TRIG] + [BANK] in grid recording opens the audio editor on the step's sample and slice; on an MKI 2026-11-14) and LAZY CHOP TEMPO (a BPM popup from the chop spacing; a personal build on an MKI read a 73.5 BPM take within 1 %, 78 % of 27 known-tempo takes within about 1 BPM offline; the final build not yet on a unit). Ten DSP effects got bit-identical speed passes (modelled, not measured on a unit; STUTTR no longer writes an M register inside its sample loop). New unit reports on an MKII (BUILD 05): the remote-commanded REMIX SWITCH boot hang is now seen three times (I110); a project reload after a demand-loader phase left the DSP frame count stopped three times; DARK REV picked on all eight tracks while MODULATION was loaded stopped the DSP in 6 of 9 replays. A host tool now loads projects and switches images over USB. 2026-11-22 (README, DSP_AUDIT (new), CYCLE_SCAN, FAILURE_MODES, TRAPS, module READMEs, remixes): no new release. A DSP audit register lists 34 techniques that make effect code shorter or cheaper with bit-identical output, applied to most DSP effects (MINIVERB's modelled cost 13.4 to 11.2 % of a frame, VERBERATION's 10.1 to 8.7 %); modelled only, not measured on a unit. The DARK REV stall (I170) was narrowed on an MKII: it needs MODULATION loaded when DARK REV starts on many tracks; a stock-effects image without the demand loader did not stall in 60 starts. Two diagnostic builds had placed SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR's stubs inside the window DARK REV writes (I188), so their results were discarded and the build now refuses such placements. Commanded REMIX SWITCH boots (I110) failed mostly while the DSP was stalled. New author reports on units: BATCH_BUGFIXES lights [BANK] for banks with trigless locks and ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS works on MIDI tracks (MKI, KYOTI release candidate), CX OSC's INDX changes the saw and triangle carriers, VOID's NBR follows the KEYBUS level (MKII). 2026-11-23 (CHANGELOG, tag v0.5, README, modules/README, fet76, vca160, keybus and morph READMEs, GLOSSARY, remix pages, FAILURE_MODES): v0.5 is the web builder's version, with three remixes. Its release check on the author's MKII left 3 of 32 program changes unapplied on octabam (INEW1); it ships with the DARK REV stall as a known fault, which octabam-verbs (no stock DARK REV) and octabam-bus (no demand loader) avoid by design but were not run against. A contributor's FET76 and VCA160 arrived after the tag; VCA160's KEY now reads a mean-square word that KEYBUS publishes for every track, so it no longer needs a hook of its own. MORPH v1.2 adds a way back (RET, CURV, END), simulator only. Most of the diff moves or shortens docs. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG, module READMEs, untagged): TEMPO BUS takes scene locks on the bus delay and reverb knobs; SCENES P2 also locks from scene B; COPY PROJECT makes stock SAVE TO NEW carry the sidecar files except .strd (I202); KITS now needs BATCH_BUGFIXES; WAVE ends every note on STOP; SHATTER gets DRV and FOLD gain compensation; THIRD_PARTY.md credits PAGE LOOP, TRACK TRIG MODE and TRIG MUTE as MIT code from Hteah/ot-mods. TRIG MUTE's docs now say stock turns a muted trig into an unmuted 8:8 trig on project load.

### OT Kyoti FW

Feature and fix builds keeping the stock feel: mute modes, pattern jump, sidechain compressor, varispeed, repitch. Tested on an MKI. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument. 2026-11-02: MUTE_MODES KEYHOLD fixes octabam#934: with SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR a muted track that had been the KEY played again once KEY moved away; held tracks now keep the post-FX cut until unmuted. Confirmed on an Octatrack MKI. 2026-11-09: RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT reloads one track's slice of the Part from the card ([BANK] + [TRACK n]) or a whole pattern ([PTN] + [BANK] + trig), landing on the next step while playing; a click from a copy with interrupts masked was fixed on the unit (I60); the REC_TRIG_MUTE fix was confirmed on hardware. 2026-11-10: octabam's HOOKS chain lets RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT and FREE LOOP share their UI-tick site in one image (emulator-checked, not flashed). 2026-11-13 (NOTES.md): BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 is being rebuilt as one packaged DSP engine for the Modwerk base (not flashed); its host check is bit-exact against the emulator twin. 2026-11-14 (README, NOTES, module README): RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT takes over the landing rules of the author's Clyps work: a reloaded track lands one tick before the step boundary, so it is never a step late; a FULL reload's sound settings change only with the first trig that sounds, never on a ringing sample; trig conditions (1:2, PRE, FILL, also after STOP and PLAY) carry on as if the saved sequence had always played. A twelfth hook at the stock trig-condition reset does this. The standalone image passed every walk-through item on the author's MKI the same day; not yet run in an octabam-built image. 2026-11-17 (README, NOTES, FLASHING, Clyps manual and scope): new CLYPS, a clip launcher after Ableton's Session view: [PTN] + [BANK] shows the active track's sequence in all 16 patterns of a bank; a trig loads one onto the track (with its sound when [FUNC] is held) while the others play on; originals, per-track temp saves and card reloads put things back. It keeps ~10 MB of sample memory and always ships with DIRECT JUMP, never beside RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT. KYOTI V1.8 (RELOAD + DIRECT JUMP) and V1.8C (CLYPS) replace V1.7; every image now carries the three bug fixes. DIRECT JUMP V7.2.2 releases tracks that SILENCE TRACKS mutes just before a jump, curing a pop on the unit (an earlier fix inferred in the emulator did not); V7.3 counts a jump's position and trig conditions from the last normal pattern change, confirmed by ear in V1.8C on 2026-11-16. 2026-11-17 (Clyps manual): a card reload of another pattern ([PTN] + [BANK] + trig) is cued by stock's CHAIN AFTER setting, or lands legato when DIRECT JUMP is on; Clyps' "x" marks only an edited sequence, never an edited Part. 2026-11-20 (README, NOTES, FLASHING, START_HERE, BUILD_KYOTI, blackpyramids-303 module README, BC handoff): new combined image KYOTI V1.8BC = V1.8C + BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 (the TB-303 voice); it gives up PLATE REV as well as SPRING REV (a project saved with either loads that FX2 as NONE) and keeps about 10 MB of sample memory. BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 now allows one voice per DSP core on every path: the machine list, TRACK PASTE, an SRC page paste and (in V1.8BC) Clyps loads refuse a second one with ONE 303 PER CORE!, and a UI-task check repairs any other way (a project saved with two keeps the lower track). Its SRC page now copies and pastes as a BLKPYRAMD; a muted BLKPYRAMD track starts no note in MUTE MODE DT-T. On a pattern or Part change the voice now carries over until the track's own first trig, ties hold across a pattern boundary, and the first note after a load gets its full GATE; before, the last step was lost, a pop could sound and the first note was a blip (found on the author's MKI in octabam test images, fixed). VARISPEED_EMUS VEM11 prices a Part switch as the overlap of old and new sounds: over the DSP budget it drops held notes to OT, then steps the new Part's engines down, and a held VARI note keeps its speed until its own next trig (it changed about 145 ms early before). Open: once, after pasting a BLKPYRAMD track into another Part's pattern, the sequencer did not advance on PLAY (not reproduced); loading a project with two voices on a core not tried on the unit. 2026-11-21 (NOTES, FLASHING, README, START_HERE, BUILD_KYOTI, octabam module READMEs): release candidates RC1-RC3 bundle three changes. VARISPEED now enters VARI at QUAN 1/1 unless the track left VARI with another QUAN, remembers that across a save and keeps a held VARI note's speed through a Part switch; its state moved out of the NEIGHBOR bytes it had shared with BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 into four Part bytes stock never edits, and older projects migrate on load. EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX also lights [BANK] for trigless locks that carry a locked value (318 B, +0.3-0.5 % CPU with [BANK] held). ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS now covers MIDI tracks (I173). Two BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 bugs found on the MKI: a 303 chosen on a FLEX track was silent (I172, fixed in RC2) and a track leaving the 303 played a burst of its FLEX sample (I174, fixed in RC3, not flashed). On 2026-11-20 VARISPEED, VARISPEED_EMUS, ERASE, BATCH_BUGFIXES and the other feature images were promoted FINAL; KYOTI V1.8 / V1.8C / V1.8BC, BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 and CLYPS wait for RC3, and their builders refuse without the WIP opt-in until then. Pin pull requests for octabam's three modules are open (octabam#1200-1202).

### STEP VIEW (Octatrack step editor)

A step editor and piano-roll pitch view for the eight MIDI tracks (MIXER + MIDI): all tracks at 32 steps a row, one track's 64 steps, notes with VEL and LEN per step. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-08. 2026-11-11: the Split view also shows the audio tracks (each step's trig and its p-locks), and Pages with the audio tracks shows the cursor track's page values beside that page's SETUP. 2026-11-12 (README): works on both sides, the 8 audio tracks and the 8 MIDI tracks (MIDI switches); YES opens a lock window with every p-lock on a step (Pitch stays MIDI only). Later on 2026-11-12: each row of the Tracks view shows only that track's own steps, with its length at the row's end (briefly a separate lengths view). 2026-11-13 (README): every row follows its own track while playing; Pages shows the cursor step's parameters underneath in the lock window's five columns; a note window for MIDI steps; FX SETUP locks through a patch to octabam's PLOCKS P2; the newest parts (lock-window layout, FX SETUP locks) are emulator-only so far. 2026-11-14 (README): the Split view became STEPS in the arranger's ARR menu, so MIXER + MIDI cycles Tracks, Pages and Pitch; track lengths are set at each row's end (SCALE PER TRACK); copy, clear and paste work in full on the audio tracks; SETUP pages show in the lock window (locked only for FX with PLOCKS P2). v0.9/v0.9.1 (2026-11-14): MIXER + MIDI toggles Tracks and Pages only; Pitch opens with a double press of a MIDI track key; the MIDI track-names feature was dropped; undo and redo up to nine steps. 2026-11-15 (README): the track number flashes M for muted MIDI tracks too; a track's length flashes when picked, and YES opens the Octatrack's SCALE window for that track. 2026-11-16 (README): the STEPS view is now called Arranger Steps; no change in function.

### AERIA OS

An operating system of its own for the Octatrack MKII, not a patch of Elektron's OS: a weather-driven multi-effect on inputs A-D (up to seven effects whose knobs the chosen weather moves) and an 8-track sequencer groovebox (sampler, sub, FM, noise, Karplus-Strong and polyphonic MIDI machines, p-locks, ratchets, per-track cellular automata), plus LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and boids as modulators. ColdFire part in C, effects in hand-written DSP56300 assembly. Installing it removes the stock OS until it is reinstalled from the card; both keep their saved data in the same battery-backed SRAM, so back up before switching. The build uses the Modwerk SDK's tools (not included); aeria-os/HARDWARE.md and AUDIO.md map the MKII for writing an OS from scratch, largely from octabam's and Modwerk's documents. Some effect folders (head, tap) are marked as someone else's work. Made with Claude Code (README). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-13. 2026-11-14: docs/CHANGELOG.md lists every release build and what was checked on the unit; docs/LOG.md is the request log of the 9-13 Nov build, with the hardware findings now on the Octatrack page and incidents I83-I86. 2026-11-20 (tag v0.9.5-beta, README, new docs/AERIA_PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md, CHANGELOG, LOG, aeria-fx test_results): the weather is trimmed to CLEAR, RAIN, FOG and AURORA (with a WX OFF switch); DIST, WIND, HAIL, TWISTER, BBD and the master EQ are gone. Builds of 2026-11-15/16 added eight MIDI tracks beside the audio tracks, a sequencer reverb bus, per-track routing to main, cue and headphones, crossfader modes, Dutch, 8 patterns and song mode, and were flashed on the unit. On 2026-11-15 a mis-encoded DSP multiply put garbage on the headphones; the build now refuses that form. After flashing the headphones were still silent (2026-11-17); v0.9.5 blames the cold-start order of the DSP clock and the output ring (a RAM boot cannot show it) and is not yet tested on the unit. New: aeria-os/sim runs the real image and both DSP programs on octabam's emulators with ten test suites; the specification lists the MKII facts used (output slot order, level lamp ids, battery RAM layout) and what only the unit can show. Cheaper effects since 2026-11-13: SMEAR with a 512 hop (1,165 -> 641 instructions a sample), VERB and AURORA at half rate (1,145 -> 736, 216 -> 165).

_Related: uses tool `modwerk` (README: the build uses tools from the Modwerk SDK and its Docker image); cites `octabam` (aeria-os/HARDWARE.md: facts sourced from octabam docs and emulator) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### OT MODS (Hteah)

Firmware mods for the Octatrack MKI built on octabam, installed by building the OS from Elektron's 1.40C file on your own computer. Two builds: full (with REC THRESHOLD, MUTE MODES, TAPE ECHO, MINI VERB and ATA WRITE GUARD by other octabam authors) and samplers only. BUILDING.md describes the method for coding agents. MIT. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14; README read.

_Related: mod for `octabam` (README: built on octabam (OCTABAM_COMMIT)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### telos (elekloader OS)

An elekloader build that is flashed once and then links more mods at every boot from a store on the unit, so new mods need no new firmware: .elemod files go over USB (SysEx with the non-commercial id 0x7D, each file read back and checked by CRC-32), and a MODS (TELOS) page at the end of SETTINGS switches them on or off for the next boot. A boot that crashes within 10 s of linking makes the next boot link nothing (one safe boot). Only +Drive-style mods (code and .bss, no patch sites). On the Digitone mk1 the store is 2 MB of raw +Drive sectors outside every area stock uses, so it never shows in Transfer; up to 63 files. Planned for the other devices elekloader supports. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-17: the Octatrack port is in the repo (octatrack/, 0.4, emulator only): .elemod files on the CF card in /ELEKLOADER/MODS (copied by USB DISK MODE or a card reader) are linked at the card's first mount, before the project load; unlike the Digitone's, these mods may patch the OS (sites), checked against stock bytes, written with interrupts masked when no task is stopped inside a site, and refused when the OS already ran them before the mount (code 23). 14 of the shop's 15 non-USB octabam conversions link together (about 61 KB); USB mods stay flash-only. DSP code from the card goes through elekloader's dspload-ot. On both devices each saved project now keeps the list of mods that ran, and loading one whose mods differ offers to switch them (LOAD PROJECT MODS?). A poc branch adds site-writing and memory-region mods for the Digitone (POC.md). 2026-11-22 (README, ar2/ and a4mk2/ README and mod.json, vendor/drive-loader-*): ports for the Analog Rytm MKII (ar2/, 0.1, OS 1.74, core-ar2 0.18) and the Analog Four MKII (a4mk2/, 0.3, OS 1.56, core-a4mk2 0.10). Both are elekloader's Drive Loaders copied unchanged into vendor/ and shipped under TELOS's name; only the SETTINGS row is TELOS's own. The module id stays drive-loader, so a build holds TELOS or the Drive Loader, never both, and +Drive mods for the Drive Loader load unchanged. Mods go to /mods through the unit's own data transfer (Elektron Transfer, Elektroid). The A4 keeps them in raw +Drive sectors that FORMAT +DRIVE empties. Projects do not yet keep their mods on either device. Neither port has run in an emulator or on a unit.

_Related: builds on `elekloader` (README: part of elekloader; built as an elekloader mod with core-dn1 and its +Drive boot linker) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-15, README (2026-11-15), README, POC.md, octatrack/README.md and design/*.md (2026-11-17), README, a4mk2/ and ar2/ README and mod.json, vendor/drive-loader-*/README (2026-11-22)_

### SuperSAW-OT

A detuned-saw track machine for one Octatrack audio track, for the Modwerk runtime, with six controls (tune, detune, mix, one to seven oscillators, width, level). A public source snapshot and test evidence only: no module or firmware, not ready to install. Before a first unit trial the base must recognise a missing module. Credits Tim Hastie, octabam and Modwerk/elekloader contributors. The author names AI coding assistance. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-16. 2026-11-19 (README): a demo video was added; still no unit trial stated. 2026-11-23 (README, README.fr, JOURNAL, REVIEW): the machine is monophonic, one instance per Part; OSC sets the oscillator count (1-7), not the voices; sub oscillator and chord mode are put off. First hardware trials ran in RAM on the author's MKII with Modwerk base 0.7.13 (see tested_note). A V0.32 source archive is posted for a Modwerk technical review; the tested package itself is private and no installable module is published. Open: missing-machine protection (SW/1), saved projects, Keep, reboot persistence.

_Related: mod for `modwerk` (README: developed for the Modwerk runtime; the snapshot belongs under sdk/drafts/supersaw/) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-16, README (2026-11-16), README, JOURNAL, REVIEW (2026-11-23)_

### ot-dpo-4ms-ensemble-folding-acid-style

Only a one-line README and a licence so far (checked 2026-11-14): an attempt to bring complex oscillators and acid filters to the Octatrack. No code, OS or loader named yet. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14. 2026-11-20 (README on main, README and docs on branch model-v0): main is now only an index; each project lives on its own branch. Branch model-v0 (2026-11-17) is a Python reference model of a bass voice for the Octatrack MKII (OS 1.40C, aimed at octabam / Modwerk as a ColdFire machine): a sine oscillator with Twist and Warp after the 4ms Ensemble Oscillator, two sub-oscillators, into OCTA303's TB-303 filter, plus alias measurements (FOLD needs 2x oversampling above about 200 Hz; CHEB is limited by table precision, not by oversampling). No firmware code yet; nothing runs on a unit.

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-14, README, model-v0 README and docs/BEFUNDE.md (2026-11-20)_
